text:
zoe: quick ux question — when you zoom into the latency heatmap, should we render the bucket aggregation boundaries (hard edges) or smooth/interpolate between buckets? i'm worried the edges read as noise at low sample rates :thinking:

matt: my gut — soften them. keep a faint edge to communicate bucketization but reduce contrast. otherwise users read the chop as perf jitter.

arie: agreed. maybe show edges only when sample rate >= 1rps or when user turns on explicit 'show buckets' in the toolbar.

sam: +1. also we should add a tiny sample-rate pill in the heatmap header (e.g., "sampled 3.2/sec") with a tooltip that explains sampling impact on edges and p95 accuracy.

zoe: love the pill idea. what about p95 line overlay? if buckets are softened the p95 can float — should it snap to bucket centers or stay continuous?

kelly: keep p95 continuous — it's more useful for trends. if users want exact bucket values we can show markers at bucket centers on hover.

matt: UX nit: make the bucket-toggle persistent per-user (local setting) not global. engineers will want to turn it on for troubleshooting without affecting everyone.

zoe: accessibility check: the current bucket line color fails AA contrast at small widths. we need to pick a higher-contrast stroke or add a 1px halo. thoughts?

arie: halo is nice because it keeps hue semantics intact. but halo + faint edge can get visually heavy. maybe use halo only when mono contrast < 4.5:1.

sam: implementation note: we can expose a CSS var for "--heatmap-edge-opacity" and compute default based on sample rate server-side. then clients can override in preferences. quick prototype in CSS: `--heatmap-edge-opacity: calc(var(--sample-rate) > 1 ? 0.18 : 0.06);`

kelly: copy for the sample-rate tooltip draft: "Observed sample rate for this view. Low sampling can make short spikes appear exaggerated; enable 'show buckets' for exact bucket counts." short and plain.

zoe: nice — also add aria-live when sample-rate changes so screen readers get a heads up after a time-range pan. small accessibility win.

design-bot: reminder: add this to the next design review agenda and attach a short before/after gif of the soften vs hard edge states.

matt: i'll make 2 quick prototypes (soft edges w/ halo, continuous p95 + hover markers) and post gifs by EOD.

zoe: thanks all — saves me from bikeshedding color choices alone. we'll review gifs tomorrow and decide defaults + preference placement. :thumbsup:
